proofs.proof_tex:
We derive the stated shrinking-overlap result from the stronger uniform theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\text{-}overlap\text{-}frontier}\).  Put \(C_T:=1+\delta_T\).  Then
\[
 q_{C_T}=\frac{\delta_T}{1+\delta_T}. \tag{38}
\]
Because \(\delta_T\to0\), for all sufficiently large \(T\) one has \(0\le\delta_T\le1\), and hence
\[
 \frac12\delta_T\le q_{C_T}\le\delta_T. \tag{39}
\]
Raising (39) to the positive power \(2(1-\beta)\) and applying the uniform theorem proves both displayed risk inequalities in the target statement, after changing only constants depending on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\).

It remains to verify the particular \(\delta_T\)-based tuning displayed in the target, since the uniform theorem uses \(q_{C_T}\).  Write
\[
 x_\delta:=T\delta_T^2,
 \qquad x_q:=Tq_{C_T}^2.
\]
By (39), \(x_q\le x_\delta\le4x_q\).  If \(x_\delta\le1\), the displayed estimator takes depth zero, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}radius\text{-}sensitive\text{-}phiw\text{-}envelope}\) gives order \(T^{-1}\).  If \(x_\delta>1\), put
\[
 k_\delta:=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log x_\delta}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the cap is inactive because \(x_\delta\le T\) eventually.  The same floor calculation as in (12)--(13), using \(q_{C_T}\le\delta_T\), gives
\[
 q_{C_T}^2\alpha^{2k_\delta}
 \le \alpha^{-2}T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)},
 \qquad
 T^{-1}L^{k_\delta}
 \le T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}. \tag{40}
\]
If the exceptional regime \(x_\delta>1\ge x_q\) occurs, then \(x_\delta\le4\), so \(k_\delta\) is bounded by a constant depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\); the envelope is again of order \(T^{-1}\).  Thus the estimator stated in the target attains its upper rate in every case.

The ratio of its second risk term to \(T^{-1}\) is \((T\delta_T^2)^{1-\beta}\).  Since \(0<\beta<1\), this proves the stated threshold and dominance claims.  The geometric variance calculation in the envelope proves that no logarithmic factor is introduced.

added_lemmas.statement:
For fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\), there is a finite constant \(A_{\mathrm{ph}}\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, simultaneously for every \(C\ge1\), every \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), and every integer \(0\le k\le\lfloor T/2\rfloor\),
\[
 E_M\!\left[(\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e))^2\right]
 \le 4M_1^2q_C^2\alpha^{2k}
       +\frac{A_{\mathrm{ph}}}{T}\{1+L^k\}.
\]
The bound is uniform in \(C\) and in all finite alphabet cardinalities.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(C\ge1\) and a member \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\).  Write
\[
 m(s,a):=E_K[Y_t\mid S_t=s,A_t=a].
\]
The conditional-moment envelope in \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}reward}\) gives \(|m(s,a)|\le M_1\), \(E_K[Y_t^2\mid S_t=s,A_t=a]\le M_2\), and hence \(|g_e(s)|\le M_1\).  These bounds are well defined for every \((s,a)\) because \(K(\cdot\mid s,a)\) is a probability kernel by \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\).

We first retain the stationary-overlap radius in the usual partial-history bias calculation.  If \(C>1\), then
\[
 \nu_C:=\frac{Cd_b-d_e}{C-1}
\]
is a probability law: it is nonnegative by \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}stationary\text{-}overlap}\), and its total mass is \((C-1)/(C-1)=1\).  Since \(q_C=(C-1)/C\),
\[
 d_b-d_e=q_C(\nu_C-d_e),
 \qquad
 \|d_b-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le q_C. \tag{1}
\]
If \(C=1\), the pointwise inequalities \(d_e(s)\le d_b(s)\), together with the fact that both laws sum to one on the finite space \(\mathcal S\), imply \(d_e=d_b\), so (1) also holds because \(q_1=0\).

On every behavior-supported action cell, \(0\le\rho_t\le L\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}policy\text{-}overlap}\); cells outside behavior support have target probability zero and use the stipulated zero convention.  Repeated conditional expectation under \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\) therefore changes the last \(k+1\) action laws from \(b\) to \(e\).  The Markov factorization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\) then gives
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)]=d_bP_e^kg_e. \tag{2}
\]
Since \(d_eP_e^k=d_e\), iteration of \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}contraction}\), followed by (1), yields
\[
 \|d_bP_e^k-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\alpha^k\|d_b-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le q_C\alpha^k. \tag{3}
\]
Integration of a function bounded in absolute value by \(M_1\) changes by at most \(2M_1\) times total variation.  Thus (2), (3), and \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}value}\) imply
\[
 \left|E_M[Z_t(k)]-\theta(K,e)\right|
 \le2M_1q_C\alpha^k. \tag{4}
\]

We next record the moment calculation, including the absence of a history-length multiplier.  The elementary inequality \(\rho_t^2\le L\rho_t\), followed successively by conditional expectation over the actions, gives
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)^2]\le M_2L^{k+1}. \tag{5}
\]
For \(1\le h\le k\), the two likelihood-ratio products in \(Z_t(k)Z_{t+h}(k)\) overlap at \(k+1-h\) action times.  At each overlap use \(\rho^2\le L\rho\); at each remaining action use likelihood-ratio cancellation.  Conditional expectation of the two rewards along the resulting Markov path produces two conditional reward means, each bounded by \(M_1\).  Since the two score means agree by behavior stationarity from \(\mathrm{ass{:}stationary\text{-}start}\), subtracting their squared common mean cannot increase the covariance upper bound.  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_M\{Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k)\}
 \le M_1^2L^{k+1-h},
 \qquad 1\le h\le k. \tag{6}
\]
For \(h\ge k+1\), the two action windows do not overlap.  The same conditional-expectation calculation expresses the cross moment as the integral of the product of two functions bounded by \(M_1\), with the intervening state law propagated for \(h-k-1\) behavior steps and the future reward regression propagated for \(k\) target steps.  Applying the total-variation contraction first to the behavior segment and then to the target segment gives
\[
 \left|\operatorname{Cov}_M\{Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k)\}\right|
 \le2M_1^2\alpha^{h-1},
 \qquad h\ge k+1. \tag{7}
\]
Equations (5)--(7) use only finite likelihood-ratio sums and the two contractions.  They therefore hold for every finite action alphabet, and their constants contain no alphabet cardinality.

Let \(N:=T-k\).  Stationarity and the finite-sum variance identity give
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{Var}_M\!\left(N^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^TZ_t(k)\right)
 &\le \frac1N\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
      +2M_1^2\sum_{h=1}^kL^{k+1-h}
      +4M_1^2\sum_{h=k+1}^{\infty}\alpha^{h-1}\right\}\\
 &\le \frac1N\left\{
      \left(M_2L+\frac{2M_1^2L}{L-1}\right)L^k
      +\frac{4M_1^2}{1-\alpha}\right\}.
 \end{split}\tag{8}
\]
The two series in (8) are geometric; in particular, no factor \(k\) occurs.  When \(k\le T/2\), \(N^{-1}\le2T^{-1}\).  Define
\[
 A_{\mathrm{ph}}:=2\left\{M_2L+\frac{2M_1^2L}{L-1}
                  +\frac{4M_1^2}{1-\alpha}\right\}<\infty. \tag{9}
\]
The strict inequalities \(L>1\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), which follow from \(\zeta>0\) and \(t_0>0\), justify both divisions in (9).  Combining the squared bias from (4) with (8)--(9) proves the asserted bound for the unclipped average.  Finally, the moment envelope gives \(\theta(K,e)\in[-M_1,M_1]\), so projection onto this interval cannot increase squared distance to \(\theta(K,e)\).  This proves the same bound for \(\widehat\theta_k\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\), and put \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\) and \(q_C=(C-1)/C\).  There are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{unif}}\le C_{\mathrm{unif}}<\infty\) and \(T_{\mathrm{unif}}<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\) and not on \(C\) or on any alphabet cardinality, such that, simultaneously for every \(C\ge1\) and \(T\ge T_{\mathrm{unif}}\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 \le C_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the observable estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}\), where \(\kappa_T(C)=0\) if \(Tq_C^2\le1\), and otherwise
\[
 \kappa_T(C):=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log(Tq_C^2)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
The converse holds against every measurable estimator.  It is witnessed by a binary-action, bounded-reward subclass of the finite-action conditional-moment model.  Hence the exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), equivalently \(C-1\asymp T^{-1/2}\) near \(C=1\), and there is no logarithmic factor in the risk.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 r:=\log(1/\alpha)=1/t_0,
 \qquad D:=2r+\log L,
 \qquad x:=Tq_C^2.
\]
Because \(t_0,\zeta>0\), one has \(r>0\), \(L>1\), and \(D>0\).  Moreover
\[
 \beta=\frac{2r}{D}=\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta},
 \qquad 1-\beta=\frac{\log L}{D}. \tag{10}
\]

For the upper bound, use \(\mathrm{lem{:}radius\text{-}sensitive\text{-}phiw\text{-}envelope}\).  Since \(0\le q_C<1\), \(x\le T\).  Thus there is a finite \(T_{\mathrm{unif}}\), depending only on \(D\), such that \(\log T/D<T/2\) for all \(T\ge T_{\mathrm{unif}}\); consequently the cap by \(\lfloor T/2\rfloor\) is inactive for every \(C\ge1\) at those sample sizes.

If \(x\le1\), then \(\kappa_T(C)=0\), and the envelope gives
\[
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_0-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le4M_1^2q_C^2+\frac{2A_{\mathrm{ph}}}{T}
 \le\frac{4M_1^2+2A_{\mathrm{ph}}}{T}. \tag{11}
\]
If \(x>1\), put \(k=\lfloor\log x/D\rfloor\).  The floor inequalities and (10) give
\[
 q_C^2\alpha^{2k}\le\alpha^{-2}q_C^2x^{-\beta},
 \qquad
 T^{-1}L^k\le T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}. \tag{12}
\]
The two quantities on the right have the same value:
\[
 q_C^2x^{-\beta}=T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}
 =T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}. \tag{13}
\]
Equations (12)--(13) and the envelope therefore imply, uniformly over the class,
\[
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le C_{\mathrm{up}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}, \tag{14}
\]
where \(C_{\mathrm{up}}\) depends only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\).  The estimator uses only \(\mathsf O_T\), the revealed policies and alphabets, and the displayed fixed constants, so (14) is a valid witness for the infimum in \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\text{-}risk}\), not an oracle family.

We next derive a testing inequality used for both lower bounds.  Let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) be mutually absolutely continuous laws with respective target values \(+a\) and \(-a\), where \(a>0\).  Put \(R=dP_+/dP_-\),
\[
 A:=\int\sqrt{dP_+dP_-},
 \qquad O:=\int\min(dP_+,dP_-).
\]
Concavity of the logarithm gives
\[
 \log A=\log E_{P_+}[R^{-1/2}]
 \ge E_{P_+}[\log R^{-1/2}]
 =-\tfrac12\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-). \tag{15}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the product of the square roots of the smaller and larger densities gives
\[
 A^2\le O(2-O)\le2O. \tag{16}
\]
For any estimator, classify as plus when its value is positive.  On either classification error its squared loss is at least \(a^2\), and the sum of the two error probabilities is at least \(O\).  Hence (15)--(16) imply
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}E_v[(\widehat\theta-va)^2]
 \ge\frac{a^2}{4}\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\}. \tag{17}
\]

For the parametric floor, take singleton observed and latent state spaces, a binary action alphabet, and \(b=e=(1/2,1/2)\).  Make the state transition constant and, independently over time, draw \(Y_t\in\{-M_1,+M_1\}\) with
\[
 \Pr_v(Y_t=y)=\frac12\left(1+\frac{y}{M_1}\frac{v}{4\sqrt T}\right),
 \qquad v\in\{-1,+1\}. \tag{18}
\]
The state contraction coefficient is zero, \(d_e=d_b\), and the action ratio is one.  Furthermore
\[
 |E_vY_t|=\frac{M_1}{4\sqrt T}\le M_1,
 \qquad E_vY_t^2=M_1^2<M_2, \tag{19}
\]
so both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) for every \(C\ge1\).  Their target values are \(\pm a_T\), where \(a_T=M_1/(4\sqrt T)\).  With \(u_T=1/(4\sqrt T)\), direct calculation and \(\log(1+z)\le z\) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_+^T\|P_-^T)
 =Tu_T\log\frac{1+u_T}{1-u_T}
 \le\frac{2Tu_T^2}{1-u_T}\le\frac14. \tag{20}
\]
The last inequality uses \(0<u_T\le1/4\).  Applying (17) yields a constant \(c_1>0\), depending only on \(M_1\), such that
\[
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\ge c_1T^{-1},
 \qquad C\ge1. \tag{21}
\]

It remains to obtain the hidden-state term uniformly in \(C\).  For \(C>1\), the amplitude in \(\mathrm{def{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}family}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac12q_C\le\varepsilon_C\le q_C. \tag{22}
\]
Indeed, if \(1<C\le2\), then \(\varepsilon_C=(C-1)/2\) and \(\varepsilon_C/q_C=C/2\in(1/2,1]\).  If \(C\ge2\), then \(\varepsilon_C=1/2\), while \(q_C\in[1/2,1)\), which again proves (22).  This argument uses no limit in \(C\).

Take the signed-depth construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}family}\), whose scaled Rademacher reward has support \(\{-M_1,+M_1\}\).  Its dimensionless emission signal is
\[
 \gamma_0:=\frac{c_0}{M_1}=\frac{1-\alpha}{4}\in(0,1/4).
\]
The stationary formulas in \(\mathrm{lem{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}membership}\) apply, and the reward moments satisfy
\[
 |E_v[Y_t\mid J_t,U_t,A_t]|\le c_0=M_1\gamma_0<M_1,
 \qquad E_v[Y_t^2\mid J_t,U_t,A_t]=M_1^2<M_2. \tag{23}
\]
Thus these alternatives belong to the conditional-moment class.  They use one observed state, the binary-action subclass of the allowed finite action alphabets, and \(2(Q+1)\) latent states.  Their target values are
\[
 \theta_v=v a_Q,
 \qquad a_Q:=c_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q. \tag{24}
\]

We expose the radius in the observed-law divergence instead of absorbing it into a constant.  Standardizing rewards by the positive number \(M_1\) is a measurable bijection of the observed experiment.  Hence the filter identities of \(\mathrm{lem{:}observed\text{-}path\text{-}kl}\), applied to \(Y_t/M_1\), give
\[
 \frac{E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]}{M_1}
 =v\gamma_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v,
 \qquad q_t^v\le K_0\alpha^Q. \tag{25}
\]
Every conditional reward probability is strictly positive because \(\gamma_0<1/4\), so all conditional divergences are well defined.  For Rademacher laws with means \(m,n\in(-1,1)\), \(\log z\le z-1\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Rad}(m)\|\operatorname{Rad}(n)\}
 \le\frac{(m-n)^2}{1-n^2}. \tag{26}
\]
The action laws are identical under the two alternatives.  The chain rule for their finite product densities, (25)--(26), and the bound \(|\gamma_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v|\le\gamma_0\) therefore give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le \frac{4\gamma_0^2\varepsilon_C^2K_0^2}{1-\gamma_0^2}
       \alpha^{2Q}\sum_{t=1}^TE[(a_t^{(Q)})^2]. \tag{27}
\]
Under the signed-depth behavior policy the actions are independent Bernoulli variables with success probability \(L^{-1}\).  With \(\ell_t=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), including every stationary initial window,
\[
 E[(a_t^{(Q)})^2]
 =L^{-(2Q-\ell_t)}\le L^{-Q}. \tag{28}
\]
Define
\[
 \overline B:=\frac{4\gamma_0^2K_0^2}{1-\gamma_0^2}<\infty. \tag{29}
\]
The inequalities \(\gamma_0<1\) and \(K_0<\infty\) justify (29), and \(\overline B\) depends only on \(t_0\).  Equations (27)--(29) prove the uniform modulus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le\overline B\,T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}. \tag{30}
\]

Choose a finite \(x_0\ge1\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\), large enough that
\[
 Q_x:=\left\lceil D^{-1}\log(8\overline Bx)\right\rceil\ge1
 \quad\text{whenever }x\ge x_0. \tag{31}
\]
By (22), (30), and \(\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}=e^{-DQ}\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q_x,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q_x,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le\overline Bx e^{-DQ_x}\le\frac18. \tag{32}
\]
The stationary depth mass satisfies
\[
 w_{Q_x}=\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^{Q_x}}{1-\alpha^{Q_x+1}}
 \ge(1-\alpha)\alpha^{Q_x}. \tag{33}
\]
The ceiling in (31) and (10) also imply
\[
 \alpha^{2Q_x}\ge\alpha^2(8\overline Bx)^{-\beta}. \tag{34}
\]
Apply (17) with (24), then use (22) and (32)--(34).  A constant \(c_2>0\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1\), satisfies, for \(x\ge x_0\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 &\ge c_2q_C^2x^{-\beta}\\
 &=c_2T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}.
 \end{split}\tag{35}
\]
The lower pair is contained in the binary bounded-reward subclass, so (35) transfers to the larger finite-action conditional-moment class by monotonicity of the supremum.

When \(x<x_0\), the hidden-state expression obeys
\[
 T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}=T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}
 \le x_0^{1-\beta}T^{-1}, \tag{36}
\]
and is therefore controlled by the parametric lower bound (21).  When \(x\ge x_0\), the maximum of (21) and (35) is at least half their sum.  This proves the lower inequality with a constant independent of \(C\).  Together with (14), it proves the displayed uniform risk law.

Finally, the ratio of the hidden-state term to the parametric term is
\[
 \frac{T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}}{T^{-1}}
 =(Tq_C^2)^{1-\beta}. \tag{37}
\]
Because \(0<\beta<1\), (37) is bounded at \(q_C=O(T^{-1/2})\) and diverges when \(Tq_C^2\to\infty\).  Also \(q_C=(C-1)/C\sim C-1\) as \(C\downarrow1\).  These identities prove the claimed elbow, the stated history length, and the absence of a logarithmic risk factor.
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem gives one cardinality- and radius-uniform minimax law joining exact stationary equality, shrinking latent overlap, and every fixed overlap radius.
added_lemmas.gap: HuWager2023 supplies the unrestricted POMDP exponent but leaves an overlapping hidden-state hard family open and does not give a stationary-overlap-radius phase diagram.
added_lemmas.consumer: In the finite-state insulin-policy adaptation, a latent physiological-occupancy assurance shortens the optimal history only through the quantitative radius \(q_C\); it yields immediate weighting at the parametric order only at the \(T^{-1/2}\) elbow.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\) be fixed, and let \(\delta_T\ge0\) be any deterministic sequence with \(\delta_T\to0\).  With \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), there are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}\le C_{\mathrm{loc}}<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{loc}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)
 \le C_{\mathrm{loc}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
An attaining observable estimator is \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T}\), where \(\kappa_T=0\) if \(T\delta_T^2\le1\), and otherwise
\[
 \kappa_T:=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log(T\delta_T^2)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
Thus the exact threshold is \(\delta_T\asymp T^{-1/2}\): when \(T\delta_T^2=O(1)\), immediate weighting has parametric order, whereas when \(T\delta_T^2\to\infty\), the required history is of order \(\log(T\delta_T^2)\) and the second risk term dominates.  There is no logarithmic factor in the risk.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After replacing bounded reward support by Hu--Wager's conditional-moment envelope, the comparison constants must be allowed to depend on the fixed envelope constants \(M_1,M_2\).  This only weakens the former constant-uniformity clause; the stronger all-\(C\) conclusion is delivered separately by \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\text{-}overlap\text{-}frontier}\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C):=\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\sigma(\mathsf O_T,\mathcal X,\mathcal A,b,e,t_0,\zeta,C,M_1,M_2)}\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}E_M[(\widehat\theta-\theta(K,e))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable estimators; \(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,b,e,t_0,\zeta,C,M_1,M_2\) are supplied, whereas \(\mathcal H,K,d_b,d_e\) are not.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The experiment must expose the finite observed and action alphabets and the Hu--Wager moment-envelope constants to the estimator while keeping every latent object unknown.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For \(0\le k<T\), define \(\widehat\theta_k:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_1,M_1]}\{(T-k)^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}Z_t(k)\}\), with \(Z_t(k)=Y_t\prod_{j=t-k}^{t}\rho_j\) and the zero-cell convention in the definition of \(\rho_t\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Under the published conditional-moment envelope the target is bounded by \(M_1\), not by one, so this is the projection that preserves the observable PHIW map and its risk guarantee.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For \(C\ge1\), define \(k_T(C):=\kappa_T(C):=0\) when \(Tq_C^2\le1\), and otherwise define \(k_T(C):=\kappa_T(C):=\min\{\lfloor T/2\rfloor,\lfloor\log(Tq_C^2)/(2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L)\rfloor\}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The optimizer balances the retained radius-sensitive bias against the overlap variance and must therefore use \(Tq_C^2\), not \(T\) alone.
The radius phase diagram is now proved, so the former open derivation handle must be replaced by the resulting computable frontier functional.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \(C>1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(X_t\) constant, \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}\), \(b(1)=1/L\), and \(e(1)=1\).  Draw a reset sign from \(\Pr(U=u)=(1+u\varepsilon_C)/2\).  If \(J_t=Q\), set \(J_{t+1}=0\) and draw a reset sign. proposed.statement:
Let \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\) be fixed, and let \(\delta_T\ge0\) be any deterministic sequence with \(\delta_T\to0\).  With \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), there are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}\le C_{\mathrm{loc}}<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{loc}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)
 \le C_{\mathrm{loc}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
An attaining observable estimator is \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T}\), where \(\kappa_T=0\) if \(T\delta_T^2\le1\), and otherwise
\[
 \kappa_T:=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log(T\delta_T^2)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
Thus the exact threshold is \(\delta_T\asymp T^{-1/2}\): when \(T\delta_T^2=O(1)\), immediate weighting has parametric order, whereas when \(T\delta_T^2\to\infty\), the required history is of order \(\log(T\delta_T^2)\) and the second risk term dominates.  There is no logarithmic factor in the risk.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing local statement is retained as a proved corollary, with its proof basis rewired to the stronger all-radius theorem and the explicit radius-sensitive envelope.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 give the PHIW upper rate on a finite-action conditional first- and second-moment class, while Theorem 6 gives the unrestricted POMDP exponent and Section 3.2 leaves distributionally overlapping hidden-state hard instances open.

Strong or square-integrable stationary density-ratio control supports root-\(T\) behavior for truncated doubly robust evaluation in fully observed MDPs, while heavier ratio tails produce slower regimes.
Latent-state density-ratio coverage is weaker than belief coverage, and future-dependent value guarantees can retain exponentially large outcome or belief quantities without the stronger conditions.
Generic partially observable off-policy evaluation can have arbitrarily large bias, while recovery in the decoupled POMDP uses invertibility and conditional-independence structure.
Double reinforcement learning attains the semiparametric efficiency bound in observed Markov models using estimated \(q\)-functions and marginalized density ratios.
Long-run average policy outcomes admit estimation and confidence intervals in a fully observed Markov mobile-health model.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Comparator positioning now rests on an all-radius extension over Hu--Wager's moment anchor, with the binary bounded family used only for lower-bound inclusion.

prose_updates.tldr: Uniformly over every \(C\ge1\), let \(q_C=(C-1)/C\).  On Hu and Wager's finite-action conditional first- and second-moment POMDP class intersected with \(d_e\le Cd_b\), the exact cardinality-uniform minimax MSE is \(T^{-1}+T^{-2/(2+t_0\zeta)}q_C^{2\{1-2/(2+t_0\zeta)\}}\), with constants independent of \(C\) and no logarithmic factor.  The exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), equivalently \(C_T-1\asymp T^{-1/2}\) near equality.  Radius-adaptive observable partial-history weighting attains the law, while a signed-depth binary bounded-reward subclass supplies the all-estimator converse and the equality endpoint supplies the parametric floor.

project_justification.gap: HuWager2023 proves PHIW upper bounds under conditional reward moments and the unrestricted POMDP minimax exponent, but its Section 3.2 leaves overlapping hidden-state hard instances open and provides no stationary-overlap-radius phase diagram.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a uniform-in-\(C\) observed-law testing modulus that joins exact stationary equality, shrinking latent stationary overlap, and every fixed overlap radius without observing the latent density ratio.
project_justification.fill: The signed-depth reset family keeps \(d_e/d_b\) within the prescribed radius and yields observed-path divergence \(T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}\), while the retained PHIW bias factor \(q_C\alpha^k\) produces a radius-adaptive history choice.  Together with the parametric pair, these calculations prove the complete uniform frontier.

sampling_model.design: One behavior-stationary trajectory from a time-homogeneous finite POMDP; randomness comes from the joint reward-transition kernel and the known behavior randomization.
sampling_model.units: The observations are \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\), with real rewards satisfying fixed conditional first- and second-moment envelopes \(M_1,M_2\); \(H_t,d_b,d_e\) remain unobserved.
sampling_model.treatment: The revealed action alphabet is any finite nonempty set and both policies are known and memoryless in \(X_t\); the matching lower bound already holds on a binary-action subclass.
sampling_model.overlap: One-step action ratios are bounded by \(e^{\zeta}\), and the unobserved joint stationary ratio is bounded by \(C\); the induced distance radius is \(q_C=(C-1)/C\), while neither stationary law nor its ratio is supplied.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No latent alphabet, transition kernel, reward regression, stationary law, proxy, emission rank, or finite-memory bound is known or estimated as a class-membership condition; the attaining estimator uses only observed rewards and revealed policy ratios.

prose_updates.related_work: HuWager2023 is the theorem anchor: its Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 analyze PHIW for general finite actions under conditional first- and second-moment bounds, its Theorem 6 proves the unrestricted POMDP exponent, and Section 3.2 asks whether the lower bound persists under distributional overlap.  The present uniform theorem intersects that published moment class with \(d_e\le Cd_b\) and answers the question for every radius at once.  Its converse is proved on a normalized, scaled Rademacher signed-depth family with binary actions and bounded rewards; that hard family is a subclass of the published moment model, so its lower bound transfers to the larger class, while the upper calculation extends over all finite actions.  MehrabiWager2025 treats observable stationary ratios in fully observed MDPs and therefore does not supply the latent-radius modulus.  ZhangJiang2024, TennenholtzShalitMannor2020, KallusUehara2020, and LiaoKlasnjaMurphy2021 mark respectively the belief-coverage, invertibility, observed-MDP efficiency, and fully observed long-run inference boundaries.  LuckettEtAl2020 and MaahsEtAl2012 motivate HuWager2023 Section 5.2; the accompanying proposition concerns only an explicitly refreshed finite discretization, not the original continuous simulator.
prose_updates.interpretation: Bounded latent occupancy helps continuously but does not by itself restore parametric precision at a fixed nonunit radius.  The hidden-state term is negligible only when \(Tq_C^2=O(1)\); beyond that elbow, the optimal observable history grows as \(\log(Tq_C^2)\).  Thus a quantitative physiological-occupancy assurance can justify shorter histories, but fixed \(C>1\) still leaves the Hu--Wager partial-observability exponent and does not replace collection of informative state or proxy measurements.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The observed-filtration posterior bound, the full stationary-initial-window KL calculation, the radius frontier, and the finite insulin-grid certificate are proved.  Remaining limitations are substantive rather than proof gaps: latent stationary overlap is imposed rather than testable from the observed trajectory, the theorem is finite-state and cardinality-uniform but does not cover the original continuous glucose simulator, and it gives mean-squared-error rates rather than confidence intervals or policy-learning regret.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The result is uniform over \(C\ge1\), all finite observed, latent, and action cardinalities, and all revealed policy pairs in the conditional-moment class; comparison constants may depend on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\) but not on \(C,T\), or cardinality.  The hard family uses binary actions, bounded scaled Rademacher rewards, and \(2(Q+1)\) latent states, so it transfers upward to the finite-action moment class but does not prove a converse under a uniformly bounded hidden alphabet.  At \(C=1\) the stationary laws coincide and immediate weighting is parametric; for fixed \(C>1\) the slower exponent remains.  The finite refreshed insulin model demonstrates the implication without asserting that the original continuous simulator satisfies finite-state contraction or latent stationary overlap.

statement_notes.justification: This local statement is the \(C_T=1+\delta_T\) specialization of the stronger uniform overlap-frontier theorem.
statement_notes.gap: The former draft treated the shrinking-radius transition as open; the uniform modulus and radius-sensitive PHIW envelope now close it.
statement_notes.consumer: Near stationary equality, it converts a substantive occupancy assurance into the exact \(T^{-1/2}\) threshold for using immediate rather than growing-history weights.
